claim: As many as 90% of all human cancers originate from epithelial tissues.
source_text: As many as 90% of all human cancers originate from epithelial tissues.
evidence_reasoning: This is a well-established fact in cancer biology presented without specific experimental data or citation in this context, drawing from general scientific knowledge.

claim: Loss of contact with proper ECM molecules results in initiation of a cell death program known as anoikis.
source_text: Conversely, loss of contact with the proper ECM molecules results in initiation of a cell death program known as anoikis (Frisch and Screaton, 2001)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by a citation to Frisch and Screaton, 2001, and represents established scientific knowledge about anoikis.

claim: Early stages of epithelial cancer progression are characterized with genetic changes that confer ability to survive and proliferate in the absence of appropriate matrix anchorage.
source_text: Early stages of epithelial cancer progression are universally characterized with genetic changes that confer ability to survive and proliferate in the absence of an appropriate matrix anchorage
evidence_reasoning: This represents established understanding in cancer biology about early cancer progression mechanisms.

claim: Tumor-derived subclones with greater metastatic capacity display increased self-aggregation in vitro.
source_text: Thus, tumor-derived subclones with greater metastatic capacity in vivo display increased self-aggregation in vitro
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to Updyke and Nicolson, 1986 and Saiki et al., 1991.

claim: Subclones selected for increased in vitro aggregation were found to be more metastatic in mice.
source_text: at the same time, subclones selected for increased in vitro aggregation were found to be more metastatic in mice (Updyke and Nicolson, 1986; Saiki et al., 1991)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: On average, 50% of all breast and lung CTCs exist in circulation as aggregates.
source_text: In particular, one report demonstrated that, on average, 50% of all breast and lung CTCs exist in circulation as aggregates (Cho et al., 2012)
evidence_reasoning: This specific quantitative claim is supported by citation to Cho et al., 2012.

claim: A gain of function screen for genes that enable proliferation independently of matrix anchorage identified PVRL4 as a cell adhesion molecule.
source_text: A gain of function screen for genes that enable proliferation independently of matrix anchorage identified a cell adhesion molecule PVRL4 (poliovirus-receptor-like 4), also known as Nectin-4.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on the experimental screen performed by the authors as described in the manuscript.

claim: PVRL4 promotes anchorage-independence by driving cell-to-cell attachment and matrix-independent integrin β4/SHP-2/c-Src activation.
source_text: PVRL4 promotes anchorage-independence by driving cell-to-cell attachment and matrix-independent integrin β4/SHP-2/c-Src activation.
evidence_reasoning: This mechanistic claim is supported by multiple experimental results presented in the manuscript, including clustering assays, signaling pathway analysis, and functional studies.

claim: Solid tumors frequently have copy number gains of the PVRL4 locus and some have focal amplifications.
source_text: Solid tumors frequently have copy number gains of the PVRL4 locus and some have focal amplifications.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by analysis of publicly available datasets as referenced in the manuscript (Cerami et al., 2012).

claim: The transformation of breast cancer cells is dependent on PVRL4.
source_text: We demonstrate that the transformation of breast cancer cells is dependent on PVRL4.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data showing effects of PVRL4 depletion on breast cancer cell transformation properties.

claim: Growth of orthotopically implanted tumors in vivo is inhibited by blocking PVRL4-driven cell-to-cell attachment with monoclonal antibodies.
source_text: Furthermore, growth of orthotopically implanted tumors in vivo is inhibited by blocking PVRL4-driven cell-to-cell attachment with monoclonal antibodies
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by in vivo experimental data presented in Figure 7 and related text.

claim: PVRL4 strongly induced anchorage-independent colony formation.
source_text: Ectopic expression of PVRL4 strongly induced anchorage-independent colony formation
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data from the colony formation assays shown in the figures.

claim: Deletion of the entire cytoplasmic region of PVRL4 did not affect its ability to promote TL-HMEC colony formation.
source_text: Remarkably, deletion of the entire cytoplasmic region of PVRL4 did not affect its ability to promote TL-HMEC colony formation (Figure 2C)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Both full-length PVRL4 and its cytoplasmic deletion mutant reduced the upregulation of squamous differentiation markers in TL-HMECs under anchorage loss conditions.
source_text: we found that both full-length PVRL4 and its cytoplasmic deletion mutant reduced this effect (Figure 2E,F)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data measuring differentiation markers shown in Figure 2E,F.

claim: PVRL4 drives rapid association of TL-HMECs into multicellular clusters in suspension.
source_text: Consistent with its role in promoting cell–cell contact formation, PVRL4 drives rapid association of TL-HMECs into multicellular clusters in suspension
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by clustering assay data presented in Figure 3.

claim: PVRL1 depletion resulted in exclusion of dsRed-labeled cells from multicellular clusters formed by PVRL4-expressing cells.
source_text: PVRL1 depletion resulted in exclusion of dsRed-labeled cells from multicellular clusters, whereas control shRNA-expressing cells were readily incorporated (Figure 3C)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by experimental data from the mixed cell clustering assay shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Stable depletion of the PVRL1 transcript abolished PVRL4-driven anchorage-independent colony formation.
source_text: Indeed, stable depletion of the PVRL1 transcript by two independent shRNA constructs (Figure 3—figure supplement 3) abolished anchorage-independent colony formation (Figure 3D)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by colony formation assay data with PVRL1 knockdown shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Cell clustering was completely abrogated in the presence of three independent PVRL4 antibodies.
source_text: Cell clustering was completely abrogated in the presence of three independent PVRL4 antibodies, whereas control IgG or a blocking antibody against E-cadherin (DECMA-1) did not produce such an effect (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 4)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by clustering assay data in the presence of antibodies.

claim: PVRL4-driven colony formation was inhibited to almost a basal level in the presence of a monoclonal antibody targeting the extracellular region of PVRL4.
source_text: PVRL4-driven colony formation was inhibited to almost a basal level in the presence of a monoclonal antibody targeting the extracellular region of PVRL4, but no such effect was observed on colonies induced by PTEN shRNA (Figure 3F)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by colony formation assay data with antibody treatment shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The PVRL4-CD8 chimeric construct containing only the extracellular domain of PVRL4 fused to CD8 transmembrane domain was sufficient to induce anchorage-independent colony formation.
source_text: Remarkably, the PVRL4-CD8tm chimeric construct was sufficient to induce anchorage-independent colony formation (Figure 4B)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by experimental data from colony formation assays with the chimeric construct.

claim: Integrin β4 physically interacts with PVRL4.
source_text: Integrin β4 physically interacts with PVRL4
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry and co-immunoprecipitation data presented in Figure 5.

claim: Depletion of integrin β4 markedly reduced PVRL4-induced anchorage-independent colony formation.
source_text: However, PVRL4-induced anchorage-independent colony formation was markedly reduced in the presence of integrin β4-specific shRNAs (Figure 5D)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by colony formation assay data with integrin β4 knockdown.

claim: PVRL4-expressing cells maintained high levels of activated SFK in suspension while control cells showed precipitous drops.
source_text: Levels of activated SFK dropped precipitously in control cells while remaining high in PVRL4-expressing cells but not in PVRL4-expressing, PVRL1-depleted cells
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by Western blot data measuring phosphorylated SFK levels shown in Figure 5E,F.

claim: PVRL4-driven anchorage-independent colony formation was abrogated in the presence of PP2, a chemical inhibitor of SFK activity.
source_text: In support of this, PVRL4-driven but not PI3K-driven anchorage-independent colony formation was abrogated in the presence of PP2, a chemical inhibitor of SFK activity (Figure 5G)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by colony formation assay data with PP2 inhibitor treatment.

claim: Two independent shRNAs against SHP-2 completely abrogated colony formation induced by PVRL4.
source_text: Indeed, two independent shRNAs against SHP-2 completely abrogated colony formation induced by PVRL4 (Figure 5H,I)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by colony formation assay data with SHP-2 knockdown.

claim: SUM190 cells contain a high-level focal amplification of the PVRL4 locus.
source_text: We first focused on an inflammatory breast tumor cell line SUM190, which contains a particularly high-level focal amplification (∼50 kb) of the
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by genomic analysis data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: RNAi-mediated depletion of PVRL4 from SUM190 cells resulted in a dramatic reduction in clonogenic survival and anchorage-independent colony formation.
source_text: RNAi-mediated depletion of PVRL4 from SUM190 cells resulted in a dramatic reduction in clonogenic survival and anchorage-independent colony formation
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data from clonogenic and colony formation assays shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Coexpression of PVRL4-CD8tm in the presence of PVRL4-targeting shRNAs alleviated the clonogenic survival defect in SUM190 cells.
source_text: Coexpression of PVRL4-CD8tm in the presence of PVRL4-targeting shRNAs alleviated the clonogenic survival defect, confirming its on-target nature (Figure 6C,D)
evidence_reasoning: This rescue experiment data confirms the specificity of the PVRL4 knockdown phenotype.

claim: Depletion of PVRL4 by RNAi from SUM190 cells resulted in a dramatic reduction in tumor growth in orthotopic xenografts.
source_text: Depletion of PVRL4 by RNAi from SUM190 (Figure 7A,B) or SUM185 (Figure 7C) cells resulted in a dramatic reduction in tumor growth
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by in vivo tumor growth data from xenograft experiments.

claim: Treatment with anti-PVRL4 monoclonal antibody resulted in remarkable stalling of tumor growth in SUM190 xenografts.
source_text: Whereas tumor volumes in the control group steadily increased over time, the PVRL4 antibody-treated group displayed a remarkable stalling of tumor growth throughout the course of the injection regimen (Figure 7D)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by in vivo tumor growth measurements with antibody treatment.

claim: PVRL4 antibody treatment resulted in a precipitous decline of PVRL4 protein levels in tumor lysates.
source_text: Immunoblotting of tumor lysates revealed that PVRL4 antibody treatment resulted in a precipitous decline of PVRL4 protein levels, suggesting that cells with the highest expression of PVRL4 were eliminated by the treatment (Figure 7E)
evidence_reasoning: The decline in PVRL4 levels is supported by Western blot data; the interpretation about elimination of high-expressing cells is an inference.

claim: Histological analysis of anti-PVRL4 antibody-treated tumors revealed areas of widespread necrosis and loss of cell contacts.
source_text: This latter observation was corroborated by histological analysis (Figure 7F), which revealed areas of widespread necrosis and, importantly, loss of cell contacts (Figure 7D–F) when compared to control IgG-treated tumors
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by histological examination data shown in Figure 7F.

claim: Anti-PVRL4 antibody was unable to efficiently recruit Fc receptor-containing cells or induce ADCC.
source_text: No increase in cell lysis was observed with anti-PVRL4 antibody over isotype control-incubated cells, demonstrating that anti-PVRL4 antibody was unable to efficiently recruit Fc receptor-containing cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 3)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by ADCC assay data showing no difference between anti-PVRL4 and control antibodies.

claim: Immunohistochemical staining revealed no differences in the extent of macrophage infiltration between control and anti-PVRL4 IgG-treated tumor sections.
source_text: Moreover, immunohistochemical staining of control and anti-PVRL4 IgG-treated tumor sections for a mouse macrophage-specific marker F4/80 revealed no differences in the extent of macrophage infiltration (Figure 7—figure supplement 4)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data comparing macrophage infiltration.

claim: Inhibiting PVRL4 in SUM190 cells does not cause EMT or select for cells with EMT-like characteristics.
source_text: In both settings E-cadherin and vimentin protein levels remained unchanged, demonstrating that inhibiting PVRL4 in SUM190 cells does not cause EMT; neither does it select for cells with EMT-like characteristics in vivo
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by Western blot data showing unchanged EMT markers, with inference about lack of EMT induction.

claim: Analysis of a publicly available dataset indicates low-level copy number gain of PVRL4 in 60.3% of breast tumor samples and high-level amplification in 7.9%.
source_text: Analysis of a publicly available dataset of copy number alterations involving PVRL4 in 484 breast tumors indicates a low-level copy number gain in 60.3% of samples, and high-level amplification in another 7.9% of samples (Cerami et al., 2012)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on analysis of published data from Cerami et al., 2012.

claim: PVRL4 has emerged as a strong predictor of poor postoperative survival of patients with breast and lung cancer.
source_text: Moreover, PVRL4 has emerged as a strong predictor of poor postoperative survival of patients with breast and lung cancer (Takano et al., 2009; Athanassiadou et al., 2011)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to clinical studies.

claim: Loss of afadin has been shown to be strongly associated with poor outcome in breast cancer patients.
source_text: Interestingly, and in contrast to PVRL4, loss of afadin has been shown to be strongly associated with poor outcome in breast cancer patients in a number of studies (Letessier et al., 2007; Fournier et al., 2011)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to published studies on afadin and breast cancer outcomes.

claim: Integrin β4 expression is associated with poor prognosis and a basal-like expression profile in breast cancer.
source_text: Similarly to PVRL4, integrin β4 expression is associated with poor prognosis and a basal-like expression profile (Diaz et al., 2005; Lu et al., 2008)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to published studies on integrin β4 in breast cancer.

claim: Targeting integrin β4 with RNAi was shown to inhibit anchorage-independent growth, invasion, and xenograft growth in breast cancer cell lines.
source_text: and targeting integrin β4 with RNAi was shown to inhibit anchorage-independent growth, invasion, and xenograft growth in breast cancer cell lines (Lipscomb et al., 2003; Bon et al., 2006)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to published experimental studies.

claim: 100% of breast tumors from patients with two or more lymph nodes that are positive for cancer cells express PVRL4.
source_text: This is particularly relevant for PVRL4 as 100% of breast tumors from patients with two or more lymph nodes that are positive for cancer cells express PVRL4 (Athanassiadou et al., 2011)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to a clinical study.

claim: PVRL4 is expressed in a limited set of normal tissues—namely, skin epidermis, hair follicles, placenta, trachea, and lung.
source_text: PVRL4 is expressed in a limited set of normal tissues—namely, skin epidermis, hair follicles, placenta, trachea, and lung (Jelani et al., 2011)
evidence_reasoning: This claim about normal tissue expression is supported by citation to Jelani et al., 2011.

claim: PVRL4 becomes overexpressed in a large fraction of breast, NSCLC, and ovarian tumors.
source_text: yet it becomes overexpressed in a large fraction of breast (Fabre-Lafay et al., 2007), NSCLC (Takano et al., 2009), and ovarian (Derycke et al., 2010) tumors
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to multiple published studies on PVRL4 expression in different tumor types.

claim: PVRL4-driven anchorage-independent growth is facilitated via activation of the integrin β4/SHP-2/Src signaling pathway in a manner dependent on cell-to-cell attachment.
source_text: Taken together, these data suggest that PVRL4-driven anchorage-independent growth is facilitated via activation of the integrin β4/SHP-2/Src signaling pathway in a manner that is dependent on cell-to-cell attachment
evidence_reasoning: This mechanistic model is inferred from multiple experimental results including knockdown studies, inhibitor experiments, and signaling measurements.

claim: Multiple oncogenic perturbations induce cell clustering in TL-HMECs.
source_text: Either expression of mutant RasV12, or myristoylated PI3K catalytic subunit (Figure 4—figure supplement 4), or shRNA-mediated depletion of PTEN (Figure 4—figure supplement 5; for depletion efficiencies see Figure 4—figure supplement 6) triggered multicellular cluster formation in TL-HMECs
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by clustering assay data with multiple different oncogenic perturbations.

claim: PVRL4-PVRL1 trans-interaction on juxtaposed cells is mechanistically involved in driving anchorage-independent growth.
source_text: The above data raise the possibility that PVRL4-PVRL1 trans-interaction on juxtaposed cells is mechanistically involved in driving anchorage-independent growth.
evidence_reasoning: This mechanistic interpretation is inferred from the combined results of clustering assays, PVRL1 depletion effects, and antibody blocking experiments.

claim: Trans-interacting PVRL4 and PVRL1 organize into zippers at sites of cell–cell contact, driving individual integrin β4 molecules into proximity sufficient for their activation.
source_text: One possibility is that trans-interacting PVRL4 and PVRL1 similarly organize into zippers at sites of cell–cell contact, driving individual integrin β4 molecules into proximity sufficient for their activation.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative mechanistic model proposed by the authors based on analogy to other cell adhesion molecules and their experimental findings.

claim: In the context of a multicellular tumor, PVRL4-PVRL1 associated signaling exemplifies a mechanism by which cell-to-cell attachment serves to mimic attachment to matrix.
source_text: In the context of a multicellular tumor, the PVRL4-PVRL1 associated signaling exemplifies a mechanism by which cell-to-cell attachment serves to mimic attachment to matrix, allowing cells to bypass the growth constraint imposed by the requirement for proper anchorage.
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretive model inferred from the experimental data showing PVRL4-driven cell-cell attachment enables anchorage-independent signaling and growth.

claim: The observed tumor growth inhibition by anti-PVRL4 antibody is likely due to direct blockade of PVRL4 function rather than immune-mediated effects.
source_text: Taken together, these data suggest that the observed inhibitory effect is likely to be a consequence of a direct blockade of PVRL4 function.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is inferred from the lack of ADCC activity and unchanged macrophage infiltration in antibody-treated tumors.
